# Introduction

Two chapters exercise the modern conservation-genomics toolkit on public whole-genome data: (1) the
new Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) genetic-diversity indicators applied to the endangered green
peafowl (*Pavo muticus*), and (2) realized-versus-masked genetic load in the inbred Scandinavian wolf
(*Canis lupus*). The cross-cutting question is not "what is the number?" but **"how fragile is the
verdict to defensible analyst choices?"** — filtering stringency, whether population structure is
modelled, the GERP threshold that defines an operational predicted-impact site class, and the
run-of-homozygosity length used as an autozygosity proxy. Where a headline moves under choices a competent analyst could each justify, we
report the movement itself as the result.

The GBF adopted a genetic-diversity target — the proportion of populations with effective size
$N_e > 500$ [@hoban2020; @mastretta2024] — that is now being operationalized by national reporters. A
central practical question is how stable that indicator is when computed from real, small-sample data.
The wolf chapter provides a contrasting, data-rich case where the source study [@smeds2022] published a
per-individual load table we can reproduce exactly, letting us separate genuine signal from analyst
sensitivity.

**Phase 5B status: COMPLETE.** This Quarto source does not
recompute the Phase-5B analyses: `load_report_values()` validates and reads the generated workflow tables
and six-row claim trace, and the render stops if a required output or column is absent. The frozen outcomes
are **15/15**, **1/4**, **0/15**, **IMPLEMENT**, **24/24**, and
**DEFER_DUPLICATES_SOURCE_STUDY**; the sections below preserve the uncertainty and scientific boundary
attached to each value. Two isolated clean-science builds, final-source reconciliation, bounded-memory
evidence, matching hashes/manifests, and no-op verification are recorded in the
[Phase-5B reproducibility record](../results/PHASE5B_REPRODUCIBILITY.md).

# Methods

## Data

- **Green peafowl** — @dong2021, Dryad `10.5061/dryad.ffbg79ctc`. Modern resequencing across three
  regional populations plus six museum specimens. After a kinship screen (below) the analysis set is
  **`{python} R.peafowl_n` unrelated individuals** across **`{python} R.population_n`**;
  Cambodia (n = 1) is dropped. A separate, geographically mismatched museum-versus-modern comparative
  callset supports a period-labelled sample contrast (`{python} R.museum_n` museum and
  `{python} R.modern_temporal_n` modern individuals after comparative-sample QC), not an estimate of
  temporal genetic erosion because period and geography are not separated by design.
- **Scandinavian wolf** — @smeds2022, Dryad `10.5061/dryad.7m0cfxpzj`. `{python} R.wolf_n` individuals with
  ancestral-allele-polarized SNPs (`INFO/AA`, two outgroups), VEP/SIFT coding annotation, and
  per-site GERP conservation scores. Individuals carry a time-period label (founding cohort ~1983
  through 2007–2014) plus outbred references (Finland, Russia, immigrants).

All empirical genomic analyses start from the deposited VCFs (no re-calling from reads). The
country-level Populations Maintained indicator starts from a versioned curated table, and the design
calibration adds transparent bounded neutral simulations. Every threshold lives in
`config/config.yaml`, and the fragility axes *are* that config made executable.

## QC and filtering (peafowl)

Two callsets are derived from a shared normalized parent (`bcftools norm -m -any`, biallelic SNPs on
the 32 autosomes): **unpruned Set A** (neutral) feeds currentNe2, while an **LD-pruned derivative of
Set A** feeds the structure analyses; **Set B** (lightly filtered, no MAF/MAC/HWE/LD-prune) feeds
diversity and preserves rare alleles. The *filtering-stringency*
knob re-derives Set A per preset — **lenient / standard / strict** (max-missing 0.7/0.8/0.9,
min-GQ 15/20/30, min-DP 4/6/8, MAC 3) — yielding **`{python} R.postmac_counts`** post-MAC sites
(a ~`{python} R.filter_spread`× spread). Per-population HWE ($P < 10^{-6}$ in any population) is applied to avoid Wahlund
false departures. A confirmatory KING kinship screen retains all `{python} R.peafowl_n` individuals.

## Contemporary $N_e$ and the fragility cube (peafowl)

The parameter sweep is `{filter} × {structure}` → `results/cube/results_cube.parquet`, with
**currentNe2** as the sole automated estimator. LD-based $N_e$ estimators read $N_e$ *out of* linkage
disequilibrium, so the un-pruned Set A is fed with a genome size of 32 Morgans (the autosome count),
invoking currentNe2's cross-chromosome ("no genetic map needed") mode [@santiago2024]; LD-pruning
would destroy the very signal being measured. The *structure* knob contrasts **modelled**
(`per_population`, the three values feeding the GBF fraction) with **ignored** (`pooled`, all 22
lumped — a Wahlund-biased cautionary contrast). NeEstimator-LDNe is a manual field-standard
comparison planned outside the DAG but **not run**; **GONE2** provides a recent-trajectory *context* panel only (a borrowed
avian recombination rate, macrochromosomes only), never the contemporary indicator [@waples2024].

## GBF indicators (peafowl)

From the cube we compute the **$N_e > 500$ indicator** (proportion of per-population estimates above
threshold, per preset) and a **robustness** table (verdict stability across presets). The
complementary **Populations Maintained (PM)** indicator is non-genomic, curated from IUCN/BirdLife
range records at country resolution; a census $N_c$ proxy contrast uses a conservative vertebrate
$N_e{:}N_c = 0.1$ [@frankham]. The three-state verdict — pass / fail / **indeterminate** (CI straddles
500, or no convergence) — is precomputed in the workflow.

## Genetic load and ROH (wolf)

Per-individual load faithfully re-implements @smeds2022's `gerp_load_polarized.py`. For each SNP the
derived allele is the non-ancestral allele (`INFO/AA`); a site enters the operational
**GERP-defined predicted-impact class** at threshold $t$ if its GERP RS score $> t$. Per individual
we accumulate, in a single per-chromosome VCF stream, GERP-weighted **realized** load ($\sum 2g$
over homozygous-derived sites in that class $/$ calls) and **masked** load ($\sum g$ over
heterozygous sites in that class $/$ calls), summing raw counts across
chromosomes. We extend the source method by sweeping the GERP threshold over **{2, 3, 4}** in one pass
— the wolf-side fragility knob — while GERP > 4 reproduces the deposit's precomputed table exactly
(Results). Runs of homozygosity are called with `bcftools roh` (GT-based HMM, a documented constant
recombination rate) and summarized as per-individual $F_{ROH}$ swept over a ROH-length cutoff, with
long ROH ($\geq 1.5$ Mb) used as a proxy for more recent autozygosity [@bertorelle2022].

## Phase-5B falsification and decision analyses

The extension was executed in a fixed order, with each independent validator acting as the next
analysis gate. For the museum–modern comparison, all-SNP estimates were paired with
**transversion-only** estimates; all $\binom{11}{5}=462$ museum-label allocations were evaluated;
six equal-$n$ modern omissions and all 11 leave-one-individual cases were retained; and uncertainty
came from 999 seeded 5-Mb chromosome-block resamples. Raw-comparative genomic opportunity remains
the denominator for $\pi$, while normalized complete-call autosomal SNPs remain the basis for
$H_o$, $H_e$, and analytically rarefied allelic richness. These checks can reduce a damage concern;
they cannot separate collection period from the deposited groups' geographic mismatch.

For the $N_e$ design analysis, neutral monoecious diploid ideal Wright–Fisher scenarios used a
shared-parent pedigree. Each offspring gamete selected one parent genome-wide; Mendelian inheritance
with Haldane recombination then operated along 32 one-Morgan chromosomes for 15 generations. Loci
were initialized in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, retained only when polymorphic in the smallest
nested sample ($n=5$), and reused in nested individual panels of 5/10/15/20/30 and balanced nested
marker panels of 250/500/1,000 for known $N_e=100/250/500/1{,}000$. Free assortment makes
cross-chromosome disequilibrium approach its drift equilibrium rapidly, which is why the
cross-chromosome currentNe2 estimate is the prespecified headline; 15 generations do not guarantee
within-chromosome drift–recombination equilibrium. Every attempt—including timeout, parse failure,
or non-convergence—passed through the same currentNe2 binary, 90% interval parser, and decision rule
as the empirical cube. The seeded pilot was repeated identically before bounded expansion.

Empirical individual/marker downsampling stayed within each real population's observed sample size
and has **unknown truth**; it is never scored correct or incorrect. Scenario Wilson intervals
quantify Monte-Carlo uncertainty across simulated replicates. At the observed empirical $n$,
repetitions necessarily reuse the single available individual subset, and lower-$n$ subsets overlap;
empirical Wilson bands therefore summarize seeded subset/marker-panel sensitivity, not independent
biological-sampling uncertainty. The scenarios calibrate this estimator/decision pipeline, not
peafowl history or a promise that an exact real sample size will resolve the indicator.

For wolves, all 211 load/ROH records were joined across the frozen 3 GERP $\times$ 5 ROH grid.
Within-cohort fractional ranks were associated with realized and masked load; cohort-stratified
bootstrap intervals and within-cohort permutations preserve the grouping structure. A partial model
controls the within-cohort rank of generic GERP-covered genotype homozygosity, providing a
predeclared mathematical-coupling check. Individual risk-proxy ranking uses the mean of $F_{ROH}$
rank, realized-load rank, and inverse masked-load rank. These remain associations among genomic
proxies, not genotype–fitness or causal inbreeding-depression estimates.

After the predeclared negative-control gate opened, ROH localization streamed the indexed wolf VCF
one chromosome at a time. For every individual and frozen GERP/ROH cell, homozygous-derived
GERP-weighted burden was partitioned inside versus outside the individual's ROH intervals and divided
by eligible polarized GERP-threshold SNP genotype calls. The partitions reconcile to Phase 4, and ROH interval unions
reconcile to $F_{ROH}$. Each of 199 seeded null replicates circularly shifts an individual's complete
set of intervals within the same chromosome, preserving chromosome and interval lengths while
sampling the fixed eligible-SNP-genotype and burden landscapes. Cohort enrichment is compared with that
position null. This tests genomic co-localization, not organismal harm or causation.

# Results

## Peafowl: diversity, structure, and temporal contrast

PCA cleanly separates the three populations (minimum centroid gap `{python} f"{R.pca_gap:.1f}"`
versus maximum within-population spread `{python} f"{R.pca_within:.1f}"`), though per-axis variance
is low (PC1 ≈ `{python} f"{R.pc1_variance:.1f}"`%) and ADMIXTURE cross-validation favours
$K$ = `{python} R.admixture_best_k` — a small-$n$ artefact, so structure is read from PCA rather than
a "best $K$". Thailand is least diverse (expected heterozygosity
`{python} f"{R.thailand_he:.3f}"`; rarefied allelic richness `{python} f"{R.thailand_ar:.2f}"`), and
Yunnan shows a heterozygote deficit ($F_{IS}$ = `{python} f"{R.yunnan_fis:.3f}"`) consistent with elevated within-population
relatedness. The museum-versus-modern temporal contrast (angle G) is **weak and metric-dependent**:
median $\pi$ and $H_o$ are marginally higher in museum specimens, but $H_e$ and
rarefied allelic richness are essentially flat. We report a geography-confounded sample contrast, not an erosion claim, with
aDNA-deamination and geographic-mismatch caveats.

![Peafowl population structure on the first two PCA axes, computed from the LD-pruned derivative of
Set A. Separation supports population-aware analysis, while low per-axis variance and small sample
sizes limit how strongly the geometry should be interpreted.](../results/figures/pca.png){#fig-pca
fig-alt="Scatterplot of peafowl samples on PCA axes one and two, coloured by population." width="90%"}

## Peafowl: damage-aware falsification {#damage-aware-falsification}

The weak temporal contrast does **not** become a temporal-erosion claim. Only
`{python} R.damage_concordant_metrics`/4 metrics retain a museum-higher direction through every
predeclared damage and individual-influence check, and exact-label p-values span
`{python} f"{R.damage_exact_p_low:.3f}–{R.damage_exact_p_high:.3f}"`. Transversion filtering retains
the sign of each metric, but $H_e$ and allelic richness are modern-higher; $H_o$ is also
single-individual-sensitive. The 5-Mb block intervals show the effect sizes rather than reducing the
result to significance labels. Most importantly, the source groups still differ in geography as
well as collection period. The defensible conclusion remains a **sample contrast with mixed metric
directions**, not temporal genetic erosion.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-damage-effects
#| tbl-cap: "Museum-minus-modern effects under all-SNP and transversion-only definitions."
R.damage_effects[[
    "variant_set", "metric", "effect_museum_minus_modern", "ci_low", "ci_high",
    "exact_permutation_p_two_sided", "direction",
]]
```

![Damage-aware museum–modern effect intervals and individual-influence diagnostics. All effects are
shown, including modern-higher and individually fragile results; the geographic mismatch remains a
design limit under every row.](../results/figures/peafowl_damage_falsification.png){#fig-damage-aware
fig-alt="Forest plot of four museum-minus-modern diversity effects for all SNPs and transversions, plus leave-one-individual influence points." width="95%"}

## Peafowl: contemporary $N_e$ and the fragility of the GBF verdict

**No population confidently passes $N_e > 500$ under any filtering preset** (`{python} R.ne_pass_by_preset`
pass for lenient / standard / strict). Verdicts are *fail* (point and 90% CI below 500) or
*indeterminate*. Under the lenient preset the cross-chromosome estimates are Yunnan
`{python} R.ne_yunnan`, Thailand `{python} R.ne_thailand`, and Vietnam `{python} R.ne_vietnam` —
the lone point above 500, but with a CI straddling it, hence
*indeterminate*, not a pass. Under stricter presets several per-population estimates fail to converge
(extreme heterozygote excess at small $n$), so convergence itself is preset-fragile (Table:
`results/tables/gbf_robustness.tsv`). Pooling across populations (structure ignored) trends low and
rises with stringency (`{python} R.pooled_ne`), below most per-population estimates — the predicted Wahlund
direction, muddied by small-$n$ noise.

The result is therefore two-sided: the **headline is robust** (`{python} R.ne_headline` pass regardless of preset), while
the **underlying estimates are fragile** (`{python} R.unstable_population_count`/`{python} R.population_count`
populations change verdict across presets; Vietnam is
estimable under lenient but not under stricter filters). The GONE2 context trajectory shows a recent
decline (approximately `{python} f"{R.gone_old:,.0f}"` → `{python} f"{R.gone_recent:,.0f}"`
over ~`{python} R.gone_generations` generations), consistent with an endangered
species but presented as context only.

![Contemporary peafowl effective-size estimates across filtering presets and population-structure
treatments. The horizontal threshold marks $N_e=500$; wide intervals and non-converged cells show
why the estimate magnitudes are fragile even though the no-confident-pass headline is stable. Only
the per-population cells feed the GBF indicator.](../results/figures/ne_cube.png){#fig-ne-cube
fig-alt="Point and interval plot of currentNe2 estimates across filters and structure treatments, with a threshold at 500." width="90%"}

## Peafowl: $N_e$ sample-design calibration {#ne-sample-design-calibration}

`{python} R.ne_design_claim` The frozen result is **0/15** simulated sample-size/marker designs resolving
both predeclared resolution truths ($N_e=250$ and $N_e=1{,}000$) under the predeclared two-sided rule; the corresponding compact design reading is
**`{python} R.ne_design_estimate`**. Correct-confident, incorrect-confident, indeterminate, and
execution-failure rates remain separate, with 95% Wilson intervals shown in the machine table.
True $N_e=500$ is treated as a boundary and is never scored as correct or incorrect. The empirical
panel is deliberately labelled sensitivity rather than validation because the true $N_e$ of those
downsampled birds is unknown, the observed-$n$ repetitions reuse individuals, and lower-$n$ subsets
overlap. No tested configuration therefore supports an exact sample-size prescription: the neutral
scenarios calibrate this estimator/decision pipeline and are not a guarantee for a future real peafowl
collection.

![Known-truth neutral scenario resolution by sampled individuals and marker density (top), separated
from observed-range empirical convergence (bottom). The empirical panel has no correctness score.
](../results/figures/peafowl_ne_design.png){#fig-ne-design
fig-alt="Heatmaps of scenario decision resolution and empirical estimator convergence across sample size and marker density." width="95%"}

## Peafowl: the two GBF indicators give contrasting, non-equivalent readings

The genomic indicator gives **`{python} R.ne_headline` sampled populations confidently classified above $N_e>500$**, whereas **Populations Maintained =
`{python} R.pm_detail`**. All three sampled populations lie
within the "maintained" set — yet none is confidently classified above the threshold. Range-wide census
(~`{python} R.census_value` mature, EN) nominally clears the $N_c \geq `{python} f"{R.nc_proxy:,.0f}"`$
proxy, but that is the wrong denominator for a
*per-population* indicator: no matched population-level census denominator is available for the
three sampled cells, and fragmentation prevents translating a range-wide total into one. **Still
present ≠ confidence that a genomic proxy clears its threshold** — the two Goal-A indicators answer
different questions and must be reported together.

## Wolf: exact reproduction, then the fragility axes

At **GERP > 4 the per-individual realized and masked loads reproduce the deposit's precomputed
`LoadPerInd.thres4` table exactly** — 95th-percentile relative error
`{python} f"{R.anchor_relative_error:.1e}"` and raw count deltas of `{python} R.anchor_deltas` across
all `{python} R.anchor_n` individuals — confirming the re-implementation is faithful before
any extension. The biological signal is recovered correctly: the inbred **Scandinavian** cohorts carry
**realized > masked** load (`{python} f"{R.scandinavian_realized_low:.3f}–{R.scandinavian_realized_high:.3f}"`
realized versus `{python} f"{R.scandinavian_masked_low:.3f}–{R.scandinavian_masked_high:.3f}"` masked),
whereas outbred references (**Finland, Russia, immigrants**) carry **masked > realized**
(`{python} f"{R.outbred_masked_low:.3f}–{R.outbred_masked_high:.3f}"` masked versus
`{python} f"{R.outbred_realized_low:.3f}–{R.outbred_realized_high:.3f}"` realized) — the masked-to-realized
group pattern reported by the source study and consistent with recessive-load exposure
[@smeds2022; @bertorelle2022]. This reanalysis does not by itself identify a causal conversion.

Both knobs move magnitude but not the pattern. Mean realized load falls `{python} R.load_means` across
GERP `{python} R.load_thresholds` (a stricter conservation filter keeps fewer, higher-confidence
sites), and mean $F_{ROH}$ falls `{python} f"{R.roh_mean_low:.3f}"` →
`{python} f"{R.roh_mean_high:.3f}"` as the ROH-length cutoff rises
`{python} f"{R.roh_low_cutoff:g}"` → `{python} f"{R.roh_high_cutoff:g}"` Mb (shifting the long-ROH
autozygosity proxy away from shorter background homozygosity). The realized-versus-masked *direction* is robust to the GERP threshold — the
wolf-side counterpart to the peafowl fragility finding: the number depends on the choice, the signal
does not.

## Wolf: individual-level association and negative control {#wolf-individual-association}

The frozen claim-trace outcome is **15/15 primary and 15/15 partial realized-load intervals above
zero**. The primary within-cohort rank association between $F_{ROH}$ and realized load is
`{python} f"{R.wolf_primary_realized_low:.3f}–{R.wolf_primary_realized_high:.3f}"` across the 15 cells.
After controlling generic GERP-covered homozygosity it remains
`{python} f"{R.wolf_partial_realized_low:.3f}–{R.wolf_partial_realized_high:.3f}"`, with
`{python} R.wolf_partial_realized_ci_positive`/15 cohort-bootstrap intervals entirely above zero.
The analogous partial masked-load association has `{python} R.wolf_partial_masked_ci_excluding_zero`/15
intervals excluding zero. Risk-proxy rankings are stable across the grid (Spearman
`{python} f"{R.wolf_rank_spearman_low:.3f}–{R.wolf_rank_spearman_high:.3f}"`; minimum tested top-set
overlap `{python} f"{100 * R.wolf_rank_overlap_low:.1f}"`%). The negative control therefore supports
proceeding to the predeclared ROH-localization test, but it does not turn proxy covariation into a
fitness or causal claim.

generic-homozygosity control.](../results/figures/wolf_froh_load_surface.png){#fig-wolf-association
fig-alt="Four heatmaps showing realized and masked load rank associations before and after controlling generic homozygosity." width="95%"}

## Wolf: ROH-localized realized burden {#wolf-roh-localization}

`{python} R.roh_localization_claim` The frozen long-ROH result is **24/24** population-by-GERP cells
beyond the null (**GERP > 2: 8/8; GERP > 3: 8/8; GERP > 4: 8/8**). At the predeclared 1.5-Mb
long-ROH cutoff, observed log2
inside/outside burden-per-eligible-genotype-call ratios span
`{python} f"{R.roh_localization_log2_low:.3f}–{R.roh_localization_log2_high:.3f}"`; the exact
cell-wise support count is `{python} R.roh_localization_support_cells`/24
(`{python} R.roh_localization_support_by_threshold`). A cell is beyond-null only when its observed
enrichment exceeds the 97.5th percentile of 199 within-chromosome circular ROH shifts **and** its
plus-one two-sided permutation p-value is at most 0.05. Every population, GERP threshold, and ROH
cutoff remains in the machine tables regardless of direction or p-value.

Inside plus outside burden, derived copies, and eligible genotype-call opportunity reconcile to the
validated Phase-4 genome-wide totals; independently rebuilt ROH unions reconcile to $F_{ROH}$. One
denominator unit is a nonmissing diploid genotype at a variant-only allSNPs record with an exact GERP
key, valid ancestral-allele polarization, and score strictly above the selected threshold. It is an
assayed-SNP opportunity denominator, not callable genomic bases; circular shifts preserve the
observed SNP/GERP landscape but cannot remove every ascertainment effect. This is localization of one
genomic risk proxy within another and therefore mechanistic support only—not measured individual
harm, fitness, causal inbreeding depression, or a management-unit result.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-wolf-roh-localization
#| tbl-cap: "Cohort ROH-localization results at the predeclared 1.5-Mb cutoff."
R.roh_localization_primary[[
    "POP", "gerp_threshold", "n_ind", "inside_eligible_genotype_calls",
    "outside_eligible_genotype_calls", "log2_enrichment", "null_ci_low", "null_ci_high",
    "permutation_p_two_sided", "beyond_null",
]]
```

`{python} R.section134_evidence`. Section 13.5 is **`{python} R.section135_decision`**—the validated

**0/1 independent annotation definitions** and **211/211 common samples**, avoiding presentation of the

one annotation definition independent of the deposited source classes, at least 0.95 common-sample
coverage, and at least 0.90 auditable callable-denominator coverage. Predicted-impact classes remain risk
proxies, not proven harmful variants. Both decisions and their numeric reopening conditions are
machine-readable and independently validated in `results/tables/phase5b_optional_decisions.tsv`.

# Limitations

We claim **risk, not demonstrated inbreeding depression**. For the peafowl, small per-population $n$
(`{python} R.population_n_compact`) yields wide $N_e$ CIs and many *indeterminate* verdicts by construction; the estimates should
not be cited as point values, and the temporal contrast is geographically narrow and aDNA-sensitive.
Both empirical chapters are **reanalyses of published data**, so the peafowl conclusion (none of the
three sampled populations is confidently classified above $N_e>500$ under the tested cells) is a
bounded indicator result rather than proof of genetic erosion, and the wolf load reproduces a published
result. The genuine contribution is methodological: a quantified demonstration that a live policy
indicator (the GBF $N_e > 500$ verdict) and a load estimate are sensitive to defensible analyst
choices, with the two non-equivalent GBF indicators shown to give contrasting readings for the same
species. GONE2 (borrowed rate) and
the ROH recombination rate (no dense wolf map) are documented approximations. The fragility cube
quantifies, rather than hides, this uncertainty.

Phase 5B does not remove the source designs' boundaries. Transversion filtering reduces one ancient-
DNA concern but cannot remove all museum-specific technical bias or the time–geography confounding.
The neutral $N_e$ scenarios use an idealized 32-chromosome pedigree with explicit linkage and
recombination, but simplify chromosome lengths, recombination architecture, and population history
and omit mutation, selection, migration, population structure, and demographic change; their
known-truth rates calibrate the implemented decision rule only. The wolf partial analysis
controls one generic-homozygosity proxy, not every possible shared denominator or cohort process.
The ROH-localization null preserves each interval's chromosome and length through circular shifts,
but it is still a genomic position null rather than an experiment or genotype–fitness design. All
Monte-Carlo failures and indeterminate outcomes remain in their denominators.

# What evidence would change the conclusion?

The limitations above are decision points, not promises to collect more data. This evidence map
identifies the next evidence or predeclared decision rule for each unresolved inference; none is required
to reproduce the present analysis.

| Current conclusion | What remains unresolved | Next evidence or decision rule | How it would change the decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| No sampled peafowl population confidently clears $N_e>500$. | Wide confidence intervals and non-convergence at population sample sizes `{python} R.population_n_compact`. | A prospectively calibrated design testing more individuals per population before relying on higher marker density; the tested landscape yielded 0/15 qualifying designs and no exact sample-size prescription. | A newly validated design could turn an indeterminate cell into pass or fail; until then, retain the three-state verdict. |
| The GONE2 trajectory is consistent with recent decline but is context only. | Peafowl linkage distances are approximated with a borrowed avian recombination rate. | A species-specific recombination map. | It would test the trajectory's timing and scale; it would not replace currentNe2 as the contemporary GBF input. |
| Genomic patterns indicate inbreeding risk, not demonstrated inbreeding depression. | The project has no direct measure of survival, fertility, or reproductive success. | Individual fitness and reproductive measurements linked to genomic inbreeding. | A genotype–fitness association could support a depression claim; load and ROH alone cannot. |
| Populations Maintained is `{python} R.pm_detail` at country resolution. | Country-level presence can hide sub-country loss and fragmentation. | Verified, time-stamped sub-country occurrence or occupancy records. | Finer records would revise the PM denominator/numerator and show whether nominally extant units retain multiple populations. |
| The $N_e$ landscape is scenario calibration, not a real-sample guarantee. | Simplified neutral truth does not reproduce peafowl history or ascertainment; empirical subsets overlap and have unknown truth. | A design resolves both simulated $N_e=250/1{,}000$ only when correct-confident Wilson lower $\geq0.70$ and incorrect-confident upper $\leq0.25$. | The observed 0/15 leaves every tested design unresolved; any real study still requires prospective empirical validation rather than importing a simulated sample-size prescription. |
| Wolf $F_{ROH}$ and realized load remain associated after the declared negative control. | Generic homozygosity is only one coupling control. | At least 12/15 partial realized-load CIs entirely above zero. | The observed `{python} R.wolf_partial_realized_ci_positive`/15 met this predeclared gate, reopening the localized-burden test; fewer than 12 would have stopped it. |
| ROH-localized burden is a genomic-proxy localization result. | Circular interval shifts do not measure survival, reproduction, or experimental causation. | Per cell, observed log2 enrichment must exceed the circular-shift 97.5th percentile and two-sided p must be $\leq0.05$; direct fitness data are required for a depression claim. | The observed `{python} R.roh_localization_support_cells`/24 long-ROH cells meet the genomic beyond-null rule. Regardless of that count, only linked fitness measurements could change the causal boundary. |
| The museum–modern result remains a contrast, not temporal erosion. | Only `{python} R.damage_concordant_metrics`/4 metrics are fully concordant and geography is confounded with period. | 4/4 metrics must retain museum-higher direction through every numerical check **and** a design must separate time from geography. | Either failure keeps the claim at contrast-only, regardless of a small p-value in one metric. |
| Wolf annotation triangulation is deferred. | The local VEP/SIFT classes duplicate the source study rather than provide independence. | At least one independent annotation definition, $\geq0.95$ common-sample coverage, and $\geq0.90$ callable-denominator coverage. | Only that numeric independence/coverage gate would justify reopening Section 13.5. |

# Reproducibility statement

All analytical results are built by the Snakemake DAG from tracked inputs: two public deposits, the
versioned curated Populations Maintained table, and transparent bounded neutral simulations. The
Streamlit explorer reads the outputs only. The [clean verification record](../results/PHASE5B_REPRODUCIBILITY.md) preserves two
isolated clean-science builds and their resource measurements, six matching science hashes, two exact
input-manifest aggregates, final-source reconciliation, and final-topology no-op results.

The report performs a render-time schema check and reads its headline analytical values from the
following workflow outputs. Missing files or columns stop the render rather than preserving stale
prose.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-report-provenance
#| tbl-cap: "Workflow outputs loaded by the report at render time."
R.provenance
```

```bash
CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64 micromamba create -n congen -f environment.lock.yml  # Apple Silicon/Rosetta
micromamba activate congen && conda config --env --set subdir osx-64
scripts/build_tools.sh                                 # currentNe2 + GONE2, pinned commits
scripts/fetch_data.sh && scripts/extract_data.sh       # Dryad data
snakemake --snakefile workflow/Snakefile phase5b --cores 4 --resources mem_mb=7000  # phases 1-5B
report/render_report.sh                                # schema-check values and render report/report.html
streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py                     # the live fragility explorer
```

Every threshold and parameter lives in `config/config.yaml`; per-phase and Phase-5B analysis gates
assert the outputs are well-formed, preserve failures/null outcomes, and reconcile figure bridges
and provenance hashes. For wolf load, the Phase-4 gate also reconciles against the deposit's own
numbers. R packages ship with the conda environment (R is conda-owned; no `renv.lock`).
